newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt volatilities steady, await FOMC.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt volatilities steady, await FOMC.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed income options were mostly steady as the market awaited the outcome of the ongoing Federal Open Market Commttee meeting, which ends on Wednesday, dealers said.

In the Chicago Board of Trade Treasury bond pit, volatilities opened strong but worked lower for most of the day back toward Monday's closing levels as futures traded narrowly around Monday's settlement.
"I'm a little bit puzzled as to why vol has come off as much as it has in front of the employment report on Friday," said a CBOT T-bond trader for a brokerage firm.

"The only argument that I could put for that is that we (March futures) are right at the concentrated strike," he noted. March T-bond futures finished up 4/32 at 112-7/32 after spending the day gyrating around 112.
The March 112 strike had the highest open interest among T-bond futures options, with 52,082 contracts for calls and 18,313 contracts for puts as of end-Monday.
Implied volatility for March T-bond futures options stood at about 10.1 percent at close, little changed from Monday but off a quarter point from early morning highs.
"We need to get away from that 112-area in order to see a return in bid," the CBOT trader said.
The shorter end of the yield curve was also calm as a majority of the market expected the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates steady when the FOMC ends Wednesday afternoon.
"I think what people are looking at now is past FOMC to Friday's employment report," said a Eurodollar trader with a brokerage firm at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
There was a lot of short February 93.75 puts -- high-gamma deals that seemed more like position-cleaning or speculation than downside protection for FOMC and jobs data, traders said.

Short-February contracts are options whose prices are based on March 1998 futures but expire in February 1997. They have high gamma values and are therefore very sensitive to futures market movements. March 1998 futures closed at 93.90.
The market also continued to see some sizable selling in out-of-the-money puts by big houses, a trend that picked up after bonds broke above a two-month-long down channel last week.
A major investment bank was said to have sold 3,000 lots of March 94.25 puts today.
Implied volatility for June Eurodollar futures options was roughly unchanged from Monday at 10.8 percent.
Traders said Eurodollar futures were likely to extend recent gains if the Fed does not make any move, pressuring front-end option implied volatilities.
But the brokerage trader added that volatilities were at around the middle of their recent ranges and would likely find bid on dips.
"If you buy it and you're right, that's great," he said. "If you're wrong, it's not going to cost you a lot of money at these levels."
